newsitem.title: CHINA: China Catholics pray for Deng as church silent.
newsitem.headline: China Catholics pray for Deng as church silent.

text.p: Chinese Catholics offered prayers for late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, with some voicing disappointment that the official church had not paid tribute at Sunday mass.
"Deng Xiaoping's death is a misfortune for us Chinese," said one believer at the Xishiku church in central Beijing.
"I hope God will take care of him," he said.
However, a priest clad in purple robes made no mention of Deng's death in his sermon to the huge congregation of Catholic faithful. Deng died on Wednesday at 92.

"I prayed in my heart but I was a little disappointed that the priest did not hold a tribute to him," said one worshipper of the diminutive communist revolutionary and atheist who ruled China for the last 18 years.
"They should have brought it up and had a minute or two of silent tribute," he said.

Deng launched China's sweeping market-oriented economic reforms and opening to the outside and ensured that Chinese had the right to worship freely in the religion of their choice, guaranteeing that liberty in the constitution.
Other worshippers said they too offered silent prayers for Deng's soul and said they believed the communist veteran would go to heaven.
"I was really moved by his death. He served the people his whole life," said one elderly woman, a believer for more than 40 years.

Nervous of independent religious activity, China has banned allegiance to the church in Rome and demands believers worship under the auspices of the officially-sanctioned China Patriotic Catholic Association.

Deng's official memorial rites on Tuesday are certain to feature careful expressions of dignified grief by top leaders but Beijing is taking pains to ensure that no unexpected outbreaks of public mourning take place.
Any religious ceremony will be excluded in a nation that is officially atheist.
